mainTopic: Ransoming a captive wife, a widow's medical costs, and the automatic כתובה clauses, especially כתובת בנין דכרין
overview: The גמרא infers from the rule in גיטין that captives are ransomed at their value even if that is more than the כתובה. A ברייתא seems to contradict this, and the גמרא answers that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds two leniencies together. Next comes a widow's medical care. The תנא קמא treats it like food paid by the orphans. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל takes fixed-cost treatment from her כתובה. רבי יוחנן advises his relatives to set a fixed fee with the doctor, and later regrets it because an אדם חשוב is different. A new משנה lists three כתובה clauses that apply even if not written: sons inherit their mother's כתובה, daughters are supported until marriage, and a widow is housed and fed, with יהודה letting heirs pay her off. The גמרא explains that כתובת בנין דכרין encourages fathers to give generous dowries, which is rooted in a פסוק, up to a tenth of the father's property. It then defines the תקנה's limits: one rule for all cases, sons only like נחלה, land only like a כתובה, no sold property, and only if a דינר is left over. The amud ends as a story about רב פפא writing his son's כתובה begins, continuing on the next amud.

steps.title: Captives are not ransomed for more than their value
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a known משנה: we do not ransom captives for more than they are worth, because of תיקון העולם.
steps.simpleTranslation: We do not redeem captives for more than their value, to protect society.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a rule from a משנה in גיטין about ransoming captives. This sets up an inference in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Overpaying for captives would encourage kidnappers to take more people. So the חכמים set a limit: pay only what a captive like this is normally worth. This is a תקנה for the good of the community.

keyTerms.meaning: The betterment of society; a rabbinic protective policy

phrases.english: One does not redeem captives
phrases.notes: This line is quoted from a משנה in גיטין (45a).

phrases.english: for more than their value,
because of the betterment of the world.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין פּוֹדִין אֶת הַשְּׁבוּיִין יוֹתֵר עַל כְּדֵי דְמֵיהֶם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens this part of the discussion on ransoming a wife by quoting an outside משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Captives are not ransomed for more than their market value, because of תיקון העולם.

steps.title: Inference: up to their value, we ransom even beyond the כתובה
steps.stepSummary: From the משנה's wording, the גמרא infers that a captive wife is ransomed at her value, even if that costs more than her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This implies that at their real value we do redeem them, even when her ransom is more than her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads between the lines of the משנה: the only limit is 'their value,' not the size of the כתובה. This inference is the setup for a contradiction in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה limits ransom only by the captive's market value. So a husband would have to pay up to that value even if it is more than his wife's כתובה. This is the point the next ברייתא will seem to contradict.

keyTerms.meaning: Marriage contract; the sum promised to the wife

phrases.english: This implies that for their value, one does redeem,

phrases.aramaic: אַף עַל גַּב דְּפִרְקוֹנָהּ יוֹתֵר עַל כְּתוּבָּתָהּ.
phrases.english: even though her ransom is more than her marriage contract.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an implied rule from the משנה quoted in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A captive wife is ransomed at her market value even if it is more than her כתובה.

steps.title: A ברייתא says the husband pays only up to the כתובה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא is raised against the inference: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says the husband ransoms her only if the price equals her כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A contradiction: If she was captured and they asked him for up to ten times her כתובה, the first time he must redeem her; after that it is up to him. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: if her ransom equals her כתובה he redeems her, and if not, he does not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that seems to clash with step 2. According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the husband never has to pay more than the כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 2 said a husband pays up to market value even beyond the כתובה. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל caps the payment at the כתובה. So the two sources seem to set different limits.

phrases.english: And a contradiction is raised:
If she was taken captive, and they were demanding from him
up to ten times her marriage contract,
the first time, he redeems her.
From here on:
if he wants he redeems her; if he wants, he does not redeem her.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיָה פִּרְקוֹנָהּ כְּנֶגֶד כְּתוּבָּתָהּ — פּוֹדָהּ,
phrases.english: If her ransom was equal to her marriage contract, he redeems her;
if not, he does not redeem her!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference from step 2 with a ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that a husband ransoms his wife at her market value even beyond her כתובה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל caps the husband's duty at the value of the כתובה, which goes against paying beyond the כתובה.

steps.title: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds both leniencies
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds two limits together: no more than market value, and no more than the כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds two leniencies.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction by saying רבן שמעון בן גמליאל agrees with the market-value limit and also adds a כתובה limit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two rules do not cancel each other out; they stack. For רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, the husband pays the lower of the two amounts. The inference in step 2 matches the view that the husband is not limited by the כתובה, while רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds that second limit.
steps.whatToRemember: For רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, a husband never pays more than market value and never more than the כתובה. Both limits apply together.

phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel
holds two leniencies.
phrases.notes: The two are: not above her market value (from the משנה in גיטין) and not above her כתובה.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל תְּרֵי קוּלֵּי אִית לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different opinions: the second limit belongs to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל alone, on top of the first.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think the market-value rule and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's כתובה rule cannot both be true.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל holds both limits; the inference that a husband pays beyond the כתובה follows the view that has only the market-value limit.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: a husband must heal his sick wife
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's rule that if a wife falls ill, her husband must pay for her healing.
steps.simpleTranslation: If she became sick, he is obligated to heal her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of our משנה to start a new topic. This sets up the ברייתא in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband's duty to pay for medical care is one of the obligations of marriage. The גמרא will now ask how this works for a widow supported from her late husband's estate.

keyTerms.meaning: To heal her (pay for her treatment)

phrases.english: If she was struck with illness, he is obligated to heal her.
phrases.notes: This is the line from our משנה on 51a.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from ransoming to a new clause in the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A husband must pay for his wife's medical treatment.

steps.title: A widow's medical costs: like food, or from her כתובה?
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא: the תנא קמא says a widow's medical costs are like food, paid by the orphans. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says treatment with a fixed cost comes out of her כתובה, and only open-ended treatment is like food.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: A widow supported from the orphans' property who needs medical care, it is like her food. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says: treatment with a fixed limit she should be healed from her כתובה; treatment with no fixed limit is like food.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא about who pays for a widow's medical care. Two opinions disagree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא puts all medical costs in the same group as food, so the orphans pay. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל splits it: a treatment with a set cost is taken from her כתובה, but ongoing treatment with no limit is like food. The difference is whether the expense has a clear end.

keyTerms.meaning: A fixed limit or set amount

steps.whatToRemember: תנא קמא: a widow's medical costs are like food (paid by the orphans). רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: fixed-cost treatment comes from her כתובה; open-ended treatment is like food.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A widow who is sustained from the property of the orphans
and needs medical treatment,
it is like sustenance.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
Treatment that has a fixed limit,
she should be healed from her marriage contract;
phrases.notes: Some versions say 'was healed' (the word in round brackets); the corrected wording is 'should be healed' (the word in square brackets).

phrases.english: treatment that has no fixed limit,
it is like sustenance.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אַלְמָנָה נִיזּוֹנֶת מִנִּכְסֵי יְתוֹמִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא that applies the משנה's medical-care rule to a widow.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תנא קמא: a widow's medical costs are like food. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל: fixed-cost treatment comes from the כתובה; open-ended treatment is like food.

steps.title: Bloodletting counts as open-ended treatment
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that in ארץ ישראל, bloodletting is treated like a medical cost with no fixed limit.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: In ארץ ישראל, bloodletting was treated like a treatment with no fixed limit.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן applies the rule of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל from the last step to one specific treatment: bloodletting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 6 we learned that open-ended treatment is like food, so the orphans pay for it, while fixed-cost treatment comes out of the כתובה. Bloodletting was done again and again in ארץ ישראל, so it goes in the open-ended group. That means the heirs pay for it, not her כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: Bloodletting, a common medical treatment in those times
Treatment with no fixed limit or set cost

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
They made bloodletting in Eretz Yisrael
phrases.notes: "They" means the חכמים. They set this as the rule.

phrases.english: like a treatment that has no fixed limit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: עָשׂוּ הַקָּזַת דָּם בְּאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the fixed versus open-ended split from step 6 to bloodletting.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Bloodletting in ארץ ישראל is open-ended treatment, so the heirs pay for it like food.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן advises his relatives to set a fixed fee
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's relatives had to care for their father's widow, who needed daily treatment. He told them to agree on a set fee with the doctor.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן's relatives had their father's wife, who needed treatment every day. They came to רבי יוחנן, and he told them: Go and fix a set amount with the doctor.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a story about how רבי יוחנן used the fixed versus open-ended rule in real life.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Daily treatment is open-ended, so the heirs would keep paying for it. Once they agree on one set fee, it becomes treatment with a fixed cost. Under step 6, that cost comes out of her כתובה, which saves the heirs money.

phrases.english: The relatives of Rabbi Yochanan
had their father's wife
phrases.notes: She is the father's widow, and the heirs have to support her.

phrases.english: who needed treatment every day.
They came before Rabbi Yochanan.
He said to them:
Go, fix a set amount for the doctor.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָרִיבֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן הֲוָה לְהוּ אִיתַּת אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A story showing how the fixed versus open-ended rule works in practice.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Setting a fixed fee turns open-ended treatment into fixed-cost treatment, which comes out of the כתובה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן regrets his advice
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says that by giving that advice, he made himself like a legal advisor coaching one side.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: We made ourselves like legal advisors who coach people with their claims.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן looks back on his advice to his relatives and regrets it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A judge or rabbi is supposed to stay neutral. By showing his relatives a way to save money at the widow's expense, he acted like a lawyer for one side. This regret sets up the גמרא's question in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Legal advisors, people who prepare claims for one side in court

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
We made ourselves like legal advisors.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי יוחנן reflects on, and regrets, the advice he gave in step 8.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Coaching one side, as רבי יוחנן did, is acting like a legal advisor, which he regretted.

steps.title: Why did רבי יוחנן change his mind?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי יוחנן was thinking at first, and what he was thinking in the end.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first, what did he hold? And in the end, what did he hold?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a question to explain רבי יוחנן's change of mind. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If giving the advice was wrong, why did he give it? And if it was right, why did he regret it? The גמרא wants the reasoning behind both of his positions.

keyTerms.meaning: What did he hold, what was his reasoning

phrases.english: At first, what did he hold,
and in the end, what did he hold?

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵעִיקָּרָא מַאי סְבַר, וּלְבַסּוֹף מַאי סְבַר?
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the advice in step 8 and the regret in step 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reasoning behind רבי יוחנן's first position and his later regret.

steps.title: Helping family versus how an important person looks
steps.stepSummary: At first he followed the פסוק about not ignoring your own family. In the end he held that an important person is different.
steps.simpleTranslation: At first he held: "And do not hide yourself from your own flesh." In the end he held: An important person is different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question and explains both sides of רבי יוחנן's thinking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His first thought was that the פסוק tells us to help our relatives, so giving them advice was a מצוה. Later he realized that when a respected leader helps his family in a way that causes someone else to lose, it looks like favoritism. So a person of his standing should hold back.

keyTerms.meaning: Do not hide yourself from your own flesh (your relatives)

steps.whatToRemember: Fixed-cost treatment comes out of the כתובה, and open-ended treatment is paid by the heirs. רבי יוחנן helped his relatives use this rule but later regretted it, because an אדם חשוב must avoid looking like he favors his family.

phrases.english: At first he held:
"and do not hide yourself from your own flesh,"
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 58:7

phrases.english: and in the end he held:
an important person is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: At first, the מצוה of helping relatives guided him. In the end, he held that an אדם חשוב must avoid the appearance of favoring his family.

steps.title: Sons inherit their mother's כתובה even if it was not written
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה: even if the husband did not write the clause that her sons will inherit her כתובה, he is still bound by it, because it is a תנאי בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If he did not write for her, "Male children you will have from me will inherit the money of your כתובה, beyond their share with their brothers," he is still obligated, because it is a condition set by the court.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches that the clause about sons inheriting their mother's כתובה applies automatically.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the wife dies first, the husband inherits her כתובה. The clause ensures that later, her own sons take that כתובה money first. After that, they split the rest of the father's estate with their half-brothers. Because the court made this clause, it works even if it was never written.

keyTerms.meaning: The כתובה clause for male children
A condition set by the court that applies automatically

steps.confusionAlert: "Their brothers" means the husband's sons from other wives. Her sons get her כתובה money on top of their regular share, and the half-brothers do not share in it.

phrases.english: MISHNAH:
If he did not write for her:
"Male children that you will have from me
will inherit the money of your marriage contract
beyond their share with their brothers,"
he is obligated, since it is a condition of the court.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא כָּתַב לָהּ בְּנִין דִּכְרִין דְּיִהְווֹ לִיכִי מִינַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה that opens a new topic: כתובה clauses that apply automatically.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The clause that her sons inherit her כתובה is a תנאי בית דין and binds the husband even if it is not written.

steps.title: Daughters are supported until they marry
steps.stepSummary: The clause that daughters live in the father's house and are fed from his property until they marry also applies automatically.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did not write, "Female children you will have from me will live in my house and be fed from my property until they are taken by husbands," he is still obligated, because it is a condition of the court.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists a second automatic clause, about supporting daughters after the father dies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the father dies, his daughters are fed from his estate until they marry. This is also a תנאי בית דין, so it applies even if the clause was left out of the כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: They will be fed and supported
By husbands, meaning until they marry

phrases.english: "Female children that you will have from me
will live in my house
and be fed from my property
until they are taken by husbands"
he is obligated, since it is a condition of the court.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second automatic clause in the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Daughters are supported from the father's estate until marriage, even if this was not written.

steps.title: A widow may live in the house and be fed
steps.stepSummary: The clause that a widow lives in her husband's house and is fed from his property during her widowhood also applies automatically.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he did not write, "You will live in my house and be fed from my property all the days you live as a widow in my house," he is still obligated, because it is a condition of the court.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה lists a third automatic clause, about the widow herself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the husband dies, his widow may keep living in his house and be fed from his estate. This also applies without being written. The next step shows that places differed on how long this right lasts.

phrases.english: "You will live in my house
and be fed from my property
all the days you live as a widow in my house"
he is obligated, since it is a condition of the court.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַתְּ תְּהֵא יָתְבָא בְּבֵיתִי וּמִיתַּזְנָא מִנִּכְסַי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third automatic clause in the משנה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A widow lives in the husband's house and is fed from his estate, even if this was not written.

steps.title: Local customs: how long the widow's right lasts
steps.stepSummary: In ירושלים and the גליל, the widow could stay for her whole widowhood. In יהודה, the heirs could pay her כתובה and end her support.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is how the people of ירושלים wrote, and the people of the גליל wrote the same way. The people of יהודה wrote: "Until the heirs want to give you your כתובה." So if the heirs want, they give her the כתובה and release her.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה ends by showing that different places wrote the widow's clause differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ירושלים and the גליל, the widow's right lasted for her entire widowhood. In יהודה, the heirs had a choice: they could pay her כתובה at any time, and then they no longer had to house or feed her.
steps.whatToRemember: Three כתובה clauses are a תנאי בית דין and apply even if not written: sons inherit their mother's כתובה, daughters are supported until marriage, and a widow is housed and fed. In יהודה, though, the heirs could end the widow's support by paying her כתובה.

phrases.english: This is how the people of Jerusalem would write.
The people of the Galilee would write
like the people of Jerusalem.
The people of Judea would write:
"Until the heirs want
to give you your marriage contract."
Therefore, if the heirs want,
they give her her marriage contract and release her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the widow's clause from step 14 was worded differently from place to place.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In ירושלים and the גליל, the widow is supported for her whole widowhood. In יהודה, the heirs may pay her כתובה and end her support.

steps.title: The reason for the clause about male sons
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: חז"ל made כתובת בנין דכרין so a father will be willing to write for his daughter a share like his son's.
steps.simpleTranslation: The גמרא: רבי יוחנן said in the name of רבי שמעון בן יוחאי: Why did חז"ל make the rule of כתובת בנין דכרין? So that a man will eagerly write a dowry for his daughter as big as his son's share.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by giving the reason behind the rule from the משנה (step 12). That rule says the woman's sons inherit her כתובה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under this rule, what a daughter brings into her marriage will end up with her own sons, the father's grandchildren. Because of that, a father is not afraid to give her a large dowry. The rule exists to encourage generous dowries.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
The כתובה rule that a woman's male sons inherit her כתובה
Literally 'jump'. Here it means to act eagerly or take the first step

phrases.english: GEMARA

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of Rabbi Shimon ben Yochai:
For what reason did they enact
the marriage-document clause about male sons?
phrases.notes: This is the rule from the משנה that the woman's sons inherit her כתובה.

phrases.english: So that a man will jump forward
and write for his daughter like his son.
phrases.notes: He writes her a dowry as large as the share his son would inherit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן יוֹחַאי: מִפְּנֵי מָה הִתְקִינוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא's discussion by giving the reason for the rule from the משנה in step 12
steps.mimraCoreRuling: כתובת בנין דכרין was made so fathers will give daughters a dowry like a son's share.

steps.title: Can the Rabbis let a daughter inherit when the Torah says she does not?
steps.stepSummary: The Torah gives inheritance to the son and not the daughter. How can חז"ל make a rule that in effect gives the daughter a large part of the estate?
steps.simpleTranslation: Is there such a thing, where the Torah says the son inherits and the daughter does not, and then חז"ל come and make a rule that the daughter does inherit?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the reason given in step 16.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If fathers are pushed to give daughters a share like a son's, the daughter is really taking part of the inheritance. That seems to work against the Torah's order of inheritance, which goes to sons.

phrases.english: And is there such a thing
where the Merciful One says
the son inherits, the daughter does not inherit,
and the Rabbis come and enact
that the daughter should inherit?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reason given in step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: The reason for כתובת בנין דכרין: encouraging a dowry like a son's share
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rabbinic rule seems to give daughters inheritance against the Torah's order of inheritance.

steps.title: Giving a daughter something also comes from the Torah
steps.stepSummary: Giving to a daughter is also based on the Torah, as the פסוק says: 'give your daughters to husbands.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This too is from the Torah, as it is written: 'Take wives and have sons and daughters, and take wives for your sons, and give your daughters to husbands.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question in step 17 by quoting a פסוק. The next steps explain how the פסוק shows this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is that providing for a daughter is not against the Torah. It has a source in the פסוק that tells a father to marry off his daughters. The גמרא still needs to show how this פסוק teaches about money, and it does that in steps 19 and 20.

phrases.english: This too is from the Torah,
as it is written:
'Take wives and have sons and daughters,'
phrases.notes: ירמיהו 29:6

phrases.english: 'and take wives for your sons,'
'and give your daughters to husbands.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא in step 17
steps.terutzResolutionType: Brings a source showing the practice is rooted in the Torah
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Giving a daughter a large share seemed to be a rabbinic change to the Torah's inheritance law.
steps.terutzMaskana: Providing for a daughter so she can marry has a basis in the פסוק.

steps.title: How can a father marry off his daughters?
steps.stepSummary: With sons, the father is in control. With daughters, how is it up to him to find them husbands?
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for sons, since that is in his hands. But daughters, is that in his hands?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the פסוק's words 'give your daughters to husbands' really mean. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A father can go and find a wife for his son. A daughter usually waits to be approached, so how can a father 'give' her to a husband? The question points to a hidden meaning in the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: They are in his hands, under his control

phrases.english: Granted sons, they are in his hands.
But his daughters,
are they in his hands?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the meaning of the פסוק quoted in step 18
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What a father can actually do to 'give' his daughters to husbands

steps.title: The פסוק means: give her clothing and money so men want to marry her
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק teaches that the father should dress her and give her something, so that men will be eager to marry her.
steps.simpleTranslation: This teaches us that he should dress her, clothe her and give her something, so that men will jump at her and come to marry her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 19. A father 'gives' his daughter to a husband by providing clothing and a dowry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This finishes the answer to step 17. Giving a daughter property is a Torah-based duty, not a break from inheritance law. Notice the same word 'קפץ' appears here as in step 16, about men being eager to marry her.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it teaches us

steps.whatToRemember: A father giving his daughter a dowry is rooted in the פסוק 'give your daughters to husbands.' That is why כתובת בנין דכרין, which encourages dowries, does not go against the Torah.

phrases.english: This teaches us
that he should dress her and clothe her
and give her something,
phrases.notes: 'Something' means property, a dowry.

phrases.english: so that they will jump at her
and come and marry her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19 and completes the answer to step 17
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק means the father must provide clothing and property so men will want to marry his daughter.

steps.title: How much must he give?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how much a father should give his daughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: And up to how much?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the size of the dowry. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that giving a dowry is established as a duty, there has to be a limit. Otherwise the daughters could take away too much of the sons' inheritance.

phrases.english: And up to how much?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how much is required by the duty set out in step 20
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The amount of property a father should give his daughter

steps.title: Up to one-tenth of his property
steps.stepSummary: אביי and רבא both say: up to one-tenth of his property.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי and רבא both say: up to a tenth of his property.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי and רבא answer step 21: the dowry goes up to one-tenth of the father's property.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This sets the measure for the dowry duty. A daughter gets real help toward marriage, and most of the estate still stays for the sons.
steps.whatToRemember: The dowry duty is measured at up to one-tenth of the father's property.

phrases.english: Abaye and Rava both say:
Up to a tenth of the property.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in step 21
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Up to one-tenth of the father's property

steps.title: Why should the sons inherit the husband's part too?
steps.stepSummary: If the goal is to encourage the bride's father to give, maybe the sons should inherit only the father's dowry, not the husband's added amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that what the father gave, they should inherit, and what the husband gave, they should not inherit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the scope of כתובת בנין דכרין. If the reason is the father's gift, why should the sons also inherit the money the husband added?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason given in step 16 was that the bride's father should give generously. So the קשיא argues the תקנה should cover only the father's dowry. The husband's part has nothing to do with that reason.

keyTerms.meaning: But say instead (proposing a different version)
The enactment that a wife's sons inherit her כתובה

phrases.english: But say: what the father gave, they should inherit,
phrases.notes: 'They' means the woman's sons, who get her כתובה under this rule.

phrases.english: what the husband gave, they should not inherit!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: דְּאָב לֵירוֹת, דְּבַעַל לָא לֵירוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the reason from step 16 (encouraging the father) to question why the husband's portion is included.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inclusion of the husband's portion in כתובת בנין דכרין
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the reason is only about the father's giving, the rule should cover only the father's dowry.

steps.title: Otherwise the father would hold back too
steps.stepSummary: If the husband's part were excluded, the father would also refuse to write a large dowry.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the father too would hold back and not write.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the husband's part must be included. Otherwise the father would also refuse to give much.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father wants his own grandchildren to benefit from the whole marriage package. If the husband's money did not pass to his daughter's sons, he would feel the deal was unfair and give less. So including the husband's portion actually serves the same goal.

phrases.english: If so,
the father too will hold back and not write.
phrases.notes: 'Write' means pledge a big dowry in the marriage document.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, אָב נָמֵי מִימְּנַע וְלָא כָּתֵב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 23.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Practical reasoning: the suggested change would defeat the purpose of the תקנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Only the father's dowry should pass to the sons
steps.terutzMaskana: Both parts pass, or the father would not give generously

steps.title: Tie the husband's obligation to the father's gift
steps.stepSummary: Then make it depend on the father: if he gave a dowry, the husband commits; if not, the husband does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say: where the father wrote, let the husband write; where the father did not write, let the husband not write!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes further with a new proposal. The husband's part should apply only when the father actually gave a dowry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 24 said the husband's part is there to encourage the father. So in a case where the father gave nothing, that reason seems missing. Why should the rule apply there?

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵימָא: הֵיכָא דִּכְתַב אָב — לִכְתּוֹב בַּעַל,
phrases.english: But say: where the father wrote, let the husband write,

phrases.aramaic: הֵיכָא דְּלָא כְּתַב אָב — לָא לִכְתּוֹב בַּעַל!
phrases.english: where the father did not write, let the husband not write!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא: הֵיכָא דִּכְתַב אָב — לִכְתּוֹב בַּעַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the answer of step 24 to suggest a case-by-case version of the rule.
steps.kashyaTarget: Applying the husband's commitment even when the father gave nothing
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the husband's part exists only to encourage the father, it is pointless when the father gave nothing.

steps.title: The Sages made one rule for everyone
steps.stepSummary: רבנן did not make distinctions between cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages did not distinguish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבנן made one uniform rule. It applies whether or not the father gave a dowry.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though the main reason fits only some cases, רבנן set a single standard for all marriages. This keeps the תקנה simple and steady.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages did not make distinctions between cases

steps.confusionAlert: This does not mean the reason is wrong. It means a rabbinic rule, once made, covers all cases even where its reason does not fully apply.

phrases.english: The Sages did not distinguish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 25.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The rule should depend on whether the father gave
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule applies equally in all cases

steps.title: Why doesn't a daughter inherit when there are sons?
steps.stepSummary: If the goal is to keep the mother's כתובה with her own children, a daughter among sons from another wife should also inherit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A daughter among the sons should also inherit?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why only sons get the mother's כתובה. A daughter is also her mother's child.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man has a daughter from one wife and sons from another wife. If the point is that a mother's money stays with her own children, the daughter should get her mother's כתובה. Why are daughters left out?

phrases.english: A daughter among the sons should also inherit?
phrases.notes: The sons here are from a different wife, so the daughter is her own mother's only child.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the amount covered to the question of who inherits.
steps.kashyaTarget: Limiting the תקנה to sons only
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the goal is to keep the mother's money with her children, a daughter is her child too.

steps.title: Modeled on regular inheritance
steps.stepSummary: רבנן made this rule like נחלה, where sons inherit and daughters do not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages made it like inheritance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבנן copied the pattern of Torah inheritance. In that pattern sons inherit, not daughters, when there are sons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Rabbinic enactments often follow a Torah model. In regular נחלה a daughter does not inherit alongside sons. So here too only sons receive the כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: They made it, they set it up

phrases.english: The Sages made it like inheritance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 27.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Modeling the תקנה on an existing Torah law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A daughter should inherit her mother's כתובה
steps.terutzMaskana: Like נחלה, sons inherit and a daughter among sons does not

steps.title: Then at least a daughter among daughters should inherit
steps.stepSummary: When all the children are daughters, daughters do inherit under נחלה, so each one should get her own mother's כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: A daughter among daughters should inherit!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the last answer to push back. When there are only daughters, they do inherit, so the rule should apply to them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the rule follows נחלה, then where daughters inherit under נחלה, they should also get their mother's כתובה. The model of step 28 seems to support daughters in this case.

phrases.english: A daughter among daughters should inherit!
phrases.notes: The man has only daughters, from different wives.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the נחלה model of step 28 into a new challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: Excluding daughters even when there are no sons
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Under נחלה daughters inherit when there are no sons, so they should get the כתובה here.

steps.title: Again, one rule for everyone
steps.stepSummary: רבנן did not distinguish. Since daughters are excluded when there are sons, they are excluded always.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages did not distinguish.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer as before. The rule was made for sons, and רבנן did not make a separate case for daughters among daughters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the general rule is 'sons, not daughters,' רבנן kept it uniform. They did not split it based on what other children happen to exist.

phrases.english: The Sages did not distinguish.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 29 with the same principle used in step 26.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Daughters among daughters should inherit their mother's כתובה
steps.terutzMaskana: The rule stays for sons only, in every case

steps.title: Why not collect it from movable property?
steps.stepSummary: Let the sons collect their mother's כתובה even from movable goods.
steps.simpleTranslation: And let it be collected from movable property?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new question. Why can this money not be collected from the father's movable property?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sons normally inherit all their father's property, movable goods included. So why should this special inheritance be limited?

phrases.english: And let it be collected from movable property?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from who inherits to what property it is collected from.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If it is like נחלה, sons inherit movables too, so they should collect from them.

steps.title: Modeled on a regular כתובה
steps.stepSummary: רבנן made it like a כתובה, which is collected only from land.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages made it like a כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that for collection, רבנן followed the rules of a regular כתובה. A regular כתובה is paid only from land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תקנה borrows from two models. For who inherits, it follows נחלה. For what it is collected from, it follows כתובה, so it comes only from land.
steps.whatToRemember: כתובת בנין דכרין follows one uniform rule (לא פלוג). It goes to sons like נחלה, and it is collected only from land like a כתובה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how רבנן build an enactment by borrowing rules from existing Torah and rabbinic laws, each for a different detail.

phrases.english: The Sages made it like a marriage contract.
phrases.notes: A regular כתובה can be collected only from land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Modeling the תקנה on an existing law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It should be collectible from movable property
steps.terutzMaskana: Like a כתובה, it is collected only from land

steps.title: Why not collect even from sold property?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the sons can't collect their mother's כתובה even from land the father sold after writing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let it be collected from sold property!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises another 'why not?' challenge. If רבנן made this rule like a real כתובה, the sons should be able to take it even from land the father already sold.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A regular כתובה is a debt, and a debt can be collected even from land the husband sold after he owed it. Step 32 said רבנן built this rule like a כתובה. So the גמרא asks: then let it work like a כתובה here too, and reach sold land.

keyTerms.meaning: Let it be collected (seized), as a creditor collects
Property that was sold but is tied to an earlier debt

phrases.english: Let it be collected from sold (liened) property!
phrases.notes: Land the father sold after he wrote the כתובה. A normal creditor could take it back from the buyer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the answer in Step 32 that the rule is modeled on a כתובה, and pushes it further
steps.kashyaTarget: The limits of כתובת בנין דכרין as modeled on a כתובה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A real כתובה reaches sold property, so this rule should too

steps.title: The משנה says 'they will inherit'
steps.stepSummary: The משנה's wording 'they will inherit' shows this works like inheritance, and nobody inherits sold property.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned in the משנה: 'They will inherit.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by pointing to one word in the משנה: 'יִרְתוּן,' they will inherit.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Heirs only receive what the father still owned when he died. Since the משנה describes the sons as inheriting, they can't take land he already sold. On this point the rule follows inheritance, not debt collection.

keyTerms.meaning: They will inherit, the משנה's wording for the sons receiving the כתובה

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that רבנן mixed features: like a כתובה it comes only from land, and like inheritance it comes only from property the father still owned.

phrases.english: We learned in the משנה: "They will inherit."
phrases.notes: The משנה quotes the condition in the כתובה: the male sons 'will inherit' the money of their mother's כתובה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 33
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reads the wording of the משנה to show this is inheritance
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since it is like a כתובה, it should reach sold property
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה calls it inheriting, and heirs cannot take sold property

steps.title: Why require an extra דינר?
steps.stepSummary: If this is inheritance, why does it only apply when at least one extra דינר is left over beyond the כתובות?
steps.simpleTranslation: But say it applies even when there is not an extra דינר left over!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges a known condition of this rule: it only works if the estate has at least one דינר more than the כתובות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The purpose of the תקנה from step 16, encouraging fathers to give generous dowries, applies just as much when nothing extra is left. So why does the rule shut off when nothing beyond the כתובות remains?

keyTerms.meaning: But say, a way of offering a different possibility
An extra דינר left over beyond the כתובות

phrases.english: But say that it applies even though
there is not an extra dinar left over!
phrases.notes: There's a known condition: the sons take their mothers' כתובות only if at least a דינר is left over for the regular inheritance.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵימָא אַף עַל גַּב דְּלֵיכָּא מוֹתַר דִּינָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another 'why not?' challenge to the limits of the תקנה, based on its purpose from Step 16, questioning the leftover-דינר condition
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The purpose of encouraging dowries applies regardless of what else is left, so the sons should get it even without an extra דינר

steps.title: רבנן would not wipe out Torah inheritance
steps.stepSummary: If nothing is left over, the rule would cancel Torah inheritance completely, and רבנן did not make their rule for that case.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where Torah inheritance would be completely uprooted, רבנן did not make this enactment.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers: the extra דינר is needed so that some normal Torah inheritance still happens.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under Torah law, all the sons share the estate equally. If the mothers' כתובות used up everything, that Torah system would disappear entirely. רבנן were willing to adjust inheritance, but not to erase it, so they only applied the rule when something is left over.

keyTerms.meaning: Inheritance as set by the Torah

steps.whatToRemember: כתובת בנין דכרין is a mix: like a כתובה it comes only from land; like inheritance it comes only from property the father still owned; and it applies only if a דינר is left, so Torah inheritance is never fully cancelled.

phrases.english: In a case where it would uproot
inheritance by Torah law,
the Sages did not make the enactment.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּמָקוֹם דְּקָא מִיעַקְרָא נַחֲלָה דְּאוֹרָיְיתָא לָא תַּקִּינוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 35 and closes the series of questions
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains a limit on rabbinic power to change Torah law
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the purpose of encouraging dowries still applies, it should apply even with nothing extra left
steps.terutzMaskana: רבנן would not make a rule that fully erases Torah inheritance

steps.title: רב פפא goes to write his daughter-in-law's כתובה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a story: רב פפא arranged a match for his son with the family of אבא סוראה and went to write the כתובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא arranged for his son to marry into the house of אבא סוראה. He went to write her כתובה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shifts to a story. This line sets the scene for what happens next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing is ruled yet. We learn who is involved: רב פפא, his son, and the bride's family, אבא סוראה. We also learn the occasion: writing the bride's כתובה.

keyTerms.meaning: Arranged a marriage, made a match

phrases.english: Rav Pappa arranged a match for his son
with the family of Abba of Sura.
He went to write her marriage contract.
phrases.notes: 'Her' means the bride, his future daughter-in-law.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב פָּפָּא אִיעֲסַק לֵיהּ לִבְרֵיהּ בֵּי אַבָּא סוּרָאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new story after the discussion of כתובת בנין דכרין ended
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets the scene: רב פפא goes to write the כתובה for his son's bride

steps.title: יהודה בר מרימר escorts רב פפא but stops at the door
steps.stepSummary: יהודה בר מרימר comes out to greet רב פפא, but at the door he starts to leave, and רב פפא invites him in.
steps.simpleTranslation: יהודה בר מרימר heard, came out, and presented himself to him. When they reached the entrance, he took leave of him. רב פפא said to him: Let the master come in with me!
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. יהודה בר מרימר walks with רב פפא out of respect, tries to leave at the door, and רב פפא asks him to come inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story is building toward something that will happen inside the house. Why יהודה בר מרימר didn't want to go in, and what happens next, comes in the following lines.

phrases.english: Yehuda bar Mareimar heard,
phrases.notes: He heard that רב פפא was coming.

phrases.english: he went out and came to present himself before him.
When they reached the entrance,
he was taking leave of him.
He said to him: Let the master come in with me!
phrases.notes: רב פפא is speaking, politely inviting יהודה בר מרימר inside.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁמַע יְהוּדָה בַּר מָרִימָר נְפַק אֲתָא אִיתְחֲזִי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story begun in Step 37
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The story continues: רב פפא invites יהודה בר מרימר to enter with him
